title: Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing
description:
At
Evolve
, we’re on a mission to make vacation rental easy for everyone. Our high-performing, customer-obsessed team runs on curiosity, communication, and accountability—working together to create exceptional experiences for our owners and guests. Whether solving big challenges, delivering outstanding results, or celebrating wins, we approach every day with purpose and passion. If you’re ready to join a mission-driven company where every teammate has the opportunity to thrive, Evolve might just be the place for you.
Why this role
As Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager, you'll own the owner lifecycle program end-to-end: the strategy, the journeys, the platform, and the results. In your first year, you'll consolidate our sending onto Customer.io, map and rebuild the journeys for each owner segment, and turn a set of disconnected sends into a measured system that drives two key metrics: qualified lead conversion and six-month owner retention. This is an owner-operator role. You'll be as comfortable building and debugging a journey in the platform and writing email copy as you are presenting strategy to leadership. We are looking for a senior individual-contributor on a small, flat team where you'll lead through clarity and evidence rather than headcount.
The team
Growth owns Evolve's owner funnel from first impression to a signed agreement and a live listing, across five programs: Attract, Convert, Launch, Nurture and Foundations. This role owns Nurture.
What you'll do
Lifecycle Strategy & Journeys
Own owner lifecycle marketing end-to-end—every scheduled and triggered message an owner receives, from their first information request through onboarding, their first 180 days, and beyond.
Audit all current and planned communications, converting findings into mapped, segment-specific journeys. Our Core, Plus, and Pro owners run distinct operations and require tailored engagement—Pro in particular needs a newly defined journey.
Expand lifecycle channels beyond email and SMS. In-product nudges, push notifications, help content, and timed sales or onboarding touchpoints should all form a cohesive journey.
Platform & Infrastructure
Lead the migration of owner communications from legacy platforms to Customer.io, establishing build standards and governance to prevent future fragmentation.
Build segmentation and triggers based on real-time behavior and performance signals (e.g., owner actions, listing status, drop-off points) rather than fixed send calendars.
Pre-Activation Nurture & Recovery
Manage pre-activation nurture and recovery, including post-information-request sequences, abandoned-lead recovery, re-engagement for unclosed sales leads, and targeted outbound campaigns.
Optimize conversion across under-engaged lead segments, ensuring structured touchpoints exist long after initial contact.
Analytics & Optimization
Drive core performance metrics, balancing lifecycle's contribution to qualified lead conversion with 180-day owner retention.
Design and run A/B tests with a stated hypothesis and a decision attached to the result, and be clear about what you learned and what you're testing next
Cross-Functional Partnership
Partner cross-functionally with sales, product, onboarding, support, and analytics to translate complex operational updates into clear owner communications.
What makes you a great fit
7+ years of experience in lifecycle, CRM, or retention marketing for consumer or prosumer audiences, with proven ownership of multi-stage journeys
Hands-on expertise with enterprise marketing automation platforms (Customer.io, Braze, Iterable, Marketo, or similar), including building, deploying, debugging, and optimizing journeys directly
Proven track record of accountability for revenue, conversion, or retention targets driven by lifecycle initiatives
Experience auditing and consolidating fragmented communication systems into a single platform and coherent architecture
Strong analytical mindset with experience segmenting audiences, analyzing cohort/journey performance, and executing hypothesis-driven A/B tests.
Exceptional copywriting skills, with the ability to write clear, engaging, human-sounding content tailored to business owners.
Experience marketing to small business owners or prosumer segments.
AI-native workflow—proficiency using modern tools (e.g., Claude) to enhance research, drafting, and analysis capabilities.
Preferred but not required
Lifecycle experience spanning pre-purchase prospect nurture through post-purchase retention.
Familiarity with Customer Data Platforms (CDPs) and collaborating with data engineering teams on event definitions and identity resolution.
Background in marketplaces, hospitality, travel, real estate, or financial services (short-term rental or property management experience is a plus).
Experience managing multi-channel surfaces alongside email and SMS, including in-product messaging and push notifications.
Basic design skills or proficiency in tools like Canva or Figma for rapid asset creation.
Compensation
For this role, compensation is based on a base salary plus a department variable annual bonus. Our base salary range is $160,000–$190,000.
Location
All Evolve team members must live in one of our approved locations by their first day. We can hire from anywhere in the U.S. except D.C. and Hawaii. Some positions may also have restrictions based on compensation in the following states: California, Maryland, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, and Washington. If you live in Colorado, you can work remotely anywhere in the state, at our downtown Denver office, or a hybrid of both! If you're planning to move soon, please let us know, and we'll be happy to review your application again.

title: Field Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
description:
Field Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
US-Remote
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer
Who We Are
At 8th Light, we bring life to the best ideas.
Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Chicago, we are a technology solutions provider that partners with organizations to solve meaningful challenges and drive sustainable growth. From early-stage startups to global enterprises, we work across industries to optimize our clients’ digital products through product strategy innovation, experiential design, AI solutions, and deep engineering expertise.
Our commitment to quality means we deliver solutions we’re truly proud of, while our curiosity sparks innovation and breakthrough thinking. 8th Lights thrive in an environment that champions continuous education, fueling our growth through mentorship and hands-on work. We foster an open, collaborative culture grounded in honesty that builds trust, and believe true success is measured by the outcomes we create for our clients.
If this kind of work and our kind of people energizes you, you’ve found the right place.
Who You Are
You’ve spent 10+ years in custom software consultancies, and you’ve been a regular presence on both sides of the business: in the room helping win the work, and in delivery helping build it. You know how to pitch a client honestly and then stand behind what you promised.
You’re highly articulate and commercially fluent. You can talk architecture with a skeptical engineering lead in one meeting and talk ROI with a client’s CEO in the next, and both walk away trusting you. You understand how technical choices shape whether a project makes money because you’ve had to make those calls yourself.
Your technical judgment comes from years of hands-on work, and you keep it current in two ways: you read widely, and you keep doing the work. “Doing” might be a few hours each week staying sharp with new tools, or it might be real delivery responsibility on a live engagement. Either way, you don’t run on knowledge that stopped accruing years ago.
You’re comfortable leading by influence rather than authority. You may not be our deepest expert on any single topic, and that’s fine, because your value shows up differently:
You ask experienced technologists the kind of sharp questions that send them back to their desk thinking.
You know a good deal across a wide range of subjects and connect ideas others keep separate.
You’re an excellent communicator, in writing and on your feet.
You bring out people’s best work through interpersonal connection and high standards.
Your name carries some weight in the communities you’re part of. When you write or speak, senior engineers pay attention, and a few of them want to come work with you.
This is primarily a market-facing role. You’d rather be out in the market shaping where we go than waiting inside for an assignment.
What You’ll Do At 8th Light
We win work by earning technical trust before a contract is ever signed, and by being genuinely present in the market the rest of the time. This role carries both. You’ll report to the CEO and work most closely with the CEO, the VP of Growth, our practice Partners, and senior technologists.
Your primary focus will require you to:
Join deal teams to help win new engagements. In a pitch that can mean proposing an architecture, shaping scope, sequencing the work into sensible stages, or recommending how to staff it. On our most important accounts, you’ll stay a technical presence the client trusts well after the work begins.
Represent us and build relationships in the market. Give talks, write, and show up in person at events. In-person presence matters here, and writing alone won’t carry the role.
Shape and sharpen what we sell. Turn what you’re seeing in the market into clearer, more current offerings, and keep our position honest: agentic products, deep platform expertise.
Work with our Growth team to help identify and build relationships with platform and AI partners that put us in front of the right work and keep our teams current.
Drive our go-to-market direction rather than wait for it. Bring a point of view and help us continuously iterate on where we should show up, what we should say, and which opportunities are worth chasing.
Internally, your footprint is lighter but real. You’re the standard other technologists measure themselves against, and you’re a mentor to those working on their business leadership and impact. You’ll weigh in from time to time on technical job standards and career pathing. You’ll start without direct reports and lead through influence, and as we grow, the role could grow into leading a small team.
Strongly Preferred Skills
We’d particularly like to hear from applicants with:
A track record of pitching and winning enterprise engagements inside a consultancy
A public technical presence: talks you’ve given, things you’ve written, communities you help lead
Experience shaping the service offerings or the technical point of view a firm takes to market
Relationships with cloud or AI platform partners, and the standing that comes with them
A working grasp of where AI and agentic tooling is heading, enough to judge where the real opportunities are
Experience mentoring senior technical talent and raising the bar around them
Compensation
Our pay range for the Field CTO role is $230,000–$287,500 USD, plus 20–30% variable compensation based on performance.
Travel Expectation
This role involves regular but not frequent travel, mostly for in-person events, client pitches, and the occasional team gatherings.
How You’ll Be Supported
At 8th Light, our culture is built on the belief that our collective growth and well-being are the drivers of our future.
Our wellness package is designed with the Whole YOU in mind and includes:
A robust L&D program featuring unlimited access to thousands of books, courses, and expert-led training on the O'Reilly learning platform.
Annual financial stipend and time allotment for learning & development
Coworking support for our global team
Flexible PTO with floating company holidays
12 weeks of new parent leave available for eligible employees
See our full list of
Benefits
.
8th Light Hubs and Geographies
8th Light’s culture is rooted in strong connections that extend across our teams, regions, and beyond client work. We are a distributed team across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, with hubs in Chicago, London, Los Angeles, New York, and Seattle.
If you are hired into a hub, you will be part of a team with regular rituals around co-working and community building. For team members outside of those cities, we offer access to coworking spaces to foster continued collaboration and connection across our global team.
We hope to see you apply!
#LI-Remote

Honesty that builds trust
— and that shapes how we approach hiring. We want you to have a clear picture of
who we are
,
what we're looking for
, and
how we handle your information
throughout the process.
Before submitting your application, please take a moment to review our
Global Candidate Privacy Notice
. By applying, you acknowledge that you've read it.

title: Senior Franchise Business Consultant
description:
Position Overview:
The Sr Franchise Business Consultant (FBC) serves as a strategic advisor and coach to a portfolio of Regional Developers within the JANPRO Systems International brand. This role provides operational guidance, financial coaching, sales and marketing alignment, training support, and process improvements to drive performance and long-term success.
Responsibilities:
Regional Developer Coaching & Business Support:
Provide ongoing coaching on staffing, financial management, workflow optimization, and revenue growth.
Facilitate meetings to review KPIs, priorities, issues, and solutions.
Identify root causes of operational challenges, develop data-driven action plans, and lead execution for measurable improvement.
Operational Excellence & Compliance
Conduct site audits to ensure adherence to brand standards and operational requirements.
Evaluate profitability, overhead costs, and operational efficiencies to strengthen margins.
Track key performance indicators to assess operational health across assigned locations.
Financial Analysis, Budgeting & KPIs:
Review business financial statements to identify gaps and improvement opportunities.
Provide annual budget guidance and assist RDs in setting realistic revenue, profit, and operational goals.
Develop, standardize, and implement systemwide KPIs and track franchisee performance.
Recommend overhead-reducing strategies and cost-optimization opportunities.
Review pricing structures and adjust margins to respond to seasonal fluctuations and demand spikes.
Process Improvement & SOP Implementation:
Create, refine, and implement standardized SOPs to ensure consistent and efficient operations.
Lead the problem-solving process from assessment through execution, ensuring solutions are effective and sustainable.
Collaborate with internal departments to streamline workflows and introduce tools that enhance scalability and efficiency.
Marketing, Sales Strategy & Alignment:
Support RDs in developing and refining local marketing plans aligned with brand goals.
Strengthen sales processes including lead management, conversion strategies, and customer engagement.
Ensure alignment between marketing initiatives, sales goals, and operational objectives.
Training & Development:
Assist in creating training materials, SOP documentation, and onboarding resources.
Train new employees with emphasis on improving sales performance and customer engagement.
Deliver group and one-on-one training sessions for new programs and ongoing performance development.
Special Projects & Collaboration:
Support initiatives related to operational enhancements, cost savings, technology rollouts, and resource development.
Collaborate with Marketing, Technology, Training, and Compliance teams to support franchisee success.
Field Visits & Reporting:
Conduct on-site visits to provide hands-on coaching and operational assessments
Prepare detailed reports summarizing findings, KPI performance, and improvement recommendations.
Maintain proactive communication with franchisees and internal stakeholders.
Qualifications:
5+ years of experience in franchising operations, franchisee coaching, business consulting, or a related field.
Bachelors degree in business or a related field is preferred
Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to develop and implement effective solutions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities independently.
Analytically minded with the ability to evaluate performance data to identify growth opportunities
Ability to travel up to 30%
Ability to maintain confidentiality and stay composed under pressure
WHO WE ARE:
Empower Brands is a leading franchise organization encompassing ten industry-leading brands across residential and commercial services: Archadeck Outdoor Living, Bumble Roofing, Canopy Lawn Care, Conserva Irrigation, FRSTeam, JAN-PRO, Koala Insulation, Outdoor Lighting Perspectives (OLP), Superior Fence and Rail, and Wallaby Windows. Empower is dedicated to providing its customers with the highest quality products and services in the home and commercial services industries while simultaneously delivering its franchise owners committed personal support, tools and empowerment to pursue their own success. Empower Brands is a portfolio company of MidOcean Partners, a leading private equity firm with an excellent track record investing in successful, growth-focused franchise businesses. title: Staff Full-Stack Engineer - Data Intensive Web-Applications - Personalization
description:
About us
AB InBev is the leading global brewer and one of the world’s top 5 consumer product companies. With over 500 beer brands, we’re number one or two in many of the world’s top beer markets, including North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, and Africa.
About AB InBev Growth Group
Created in 2022, the Growth Group unifies our business-to-business (B2B), direct-to-consumer (DTC), Sales & Distribution, and Marketing teams. By bringing together global tech and commercial functions, the Growth Group allows us to fully leverage data and drive digital transformation and organic growth for AB InBev around the world.
In addition to supporting well known global beer brands like Corona, Budweiser and Michelob Ultra, the Growth Group is home to a robust suite of digital products including our B2B digital commerce platform BEES, on-demand delivery services Ze Delivery and TaDa Delivery, and table top beer keg PerfectDraft.
We are an exceptional team, focused on understanding and supporting consumer and customer needs, harnessing new technology, and scaling growth opportunities.
About the Role:
As a Staff Full Stack Engineer (Backend Focus), you will build and operate the backend of a Web Analytics and AI portal. That includes the APIs that serve the application, the read data layer over analytical data, authentication and authorization, and the integration points with the services the rest of the team builds. The portal gives commercial intelligence to the people who make business decisions, through daily briefings, customizable KPIs, analytical insights, geographic exploration, and conversational analytics.
This is a Staff (L6), hands-on individual contributor role on a lean team where everyone is Staff: a Staff Architect, Staff AI Engineers, Staff Software Engineers, and Data Engineers. Architectural direction sits with the Staff Architect, and the AI Engineers own the agents. You are the builder: you take features from the design doc to production, end to end, and you make them fast, observable, and reliable. Most of your time goes to writing, reviewing, and operating code, including the user interface when the delivery calls for it.
What you'll do:
Build the backend and ship features end to end
Design, implement, test, and operate backend services against explicit latency, availability, and cost targets.
Implement typed, versioned API contracts and evolve them without breaking clients.
Own authentication, authorization, and multi-tenant access control across the portal.
Ship features end to end, from the API to the interface, when the delivery calls for it.
Integrate the application with internal services, including the agent services built by the AI Engineers. This covers response streaming, timeouts, cancellation, and partial failures.
Own the read path and performance
Own the read path over analytical data: data modeling, query plans, pagination, batching, caching, and consistency trade-offs.
Set and defend performance budgets. Profile services, reduce tail latency (p95, p99), and optimize cost per request.
Run load and capacity tests before launches, and use the results to make design decisions.
Make systems observable and reliable
Instrument services with metrics, structured logs, and distributed tracing from day one.
Define SLIs and SLOs, alerts, and dashboards for the components you own, and take part in on-call.
Diagnose and fix reliability issues, and lead incident response and blameless postmortems.
Establish safe rollout practices: feature flags, canary releases, and fast rollback.
Design and raise the bar
Write design docs for the components you deliver, compare alternatives with data and prototypes, and escalate risk to the Staff Architect.
Raise the team's technical bar through code review, pairing, and standards for testing, observability, and safe rollout.
Use coding agent harnesses such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex as part of your workflow, and review generated code against tests, types, and contracts.
What you'll need:
Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, or another quantitative field. A master's degree or PhD is a plus.
Relevant experience designing, building, and operating distributed backend services in production, across coding standards, code review, build, automated testing, deployment, and operations.
A track record of building features end-to-end and owning them in production.
Relevant experience in software design for reliability and scale, on both new and existing systems.
Deep command of at least one high-performance language, such as Java/Kotlin, Go, Rust, C++, or C#, including its memory model, concurrency model, and runtime.
Ability to work productively in Python, the language of the current services.
Hands-on experience with observability in production: metrics, tracing, logging, SLOs, and tools such as OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Grafana, or Prometheus.
Proven experience with performance work: profiling, query optimization, caching strategies, and load testing.
Production depth in distributed systems: timeouts, retries, idempotency, partial failure, streaming (SSE, WebSockets), and decisions based on tail latency (p95, p99).
Relevant experience delivering full stack to production with TypeScript and a modern web framework.
Day-to-day fluency with coding agent harnesses such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex, including critical review of generated code.
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to discuss architecture and trade-offs in depth.
Advanced communication in English; Spanish is a plus.
Nice to have:
Experience with serving layers for analytical data (OLAP, columnar stores, semantic layers) or with data platform integration.
Experience integrating applications with LLM or agent services as a consumer.
Experience with B2B, multi-country, or multi-tenant products.
Experience with cloud (Azure, AWS, or GCP), containers, and Kubernetes.
More about you:
You are a builder: you like taking a feature from a blank page to production and owning it from then on.
You spend most of your time writing, reviewing, and operating code.
You treat observability and performance as part of the feature, not something added afterward.
You influence architecture with evidence: measurements, prototypes, and explicit trade-offs.
You go from the API to the interface when the feature needs it.
You use tests, types, and contracts as the guardrails for your code and for generated code.
You work well on a staff-level team where everyone operates what they ship.

description:
The Role
You'll own the revenue and Annual Revenue Run Rate (ARRR) models that power Everlaw’s top-line forecasting, bringing clarity and speed to our business planning and operating visibility. Sitting at the intersection of FP&A, GTM, Accounting, and Enterprise Technology, you will turn complex customer and contract data into clear financial models, variance analyses, and actionable insights that support strategic decisions across the company.
This is a full-time, exempt position based in our Oakland, CA office with a hybrid work schedule: in office M/W/Th with the option to work from home on Tu/Fr.
What you'll do
Build, refine, and automate Everlaw’s revenue and ARRR forecasting models to improve accuracy, scalability, and recurring reporting workflows.
Deliver monthly and quarterly reporting on ARRR, expansions, renewals, churn, customer cohorts, and key revenue metrics.
Analyze actual financial results against forecasts and plans, investigating material variances to their root causes and explaining key drivers to leadership.
Partner with Accounting, RevOps, and Enterprise Technology to reconcile revenue data, validate inputs, and strengthen underlying data structures and controls.
Support annual budgeting, quarterly rolling forecasts, and executive and Board reporting with well-documented assumptions and timely financial materials.
About You
You have at least 3 years of experience in FP&A, revenue finance, or financial analysis, ideally supporting revenue planning or recurring-revenue metrics in a SaaS environment.
You bring advanced financial modeling skills in Excel or Google Sheets, with a focus on building transparent, automated, and easy-to-maintain models.
You are an analytical problem solver who can navigate complex customer and contract data, investigate data issues, and reconcile disparate data sources.
You communicate complex financial concepts clearly and concisely to both finance and non-finance business partners.
You thrive in cross-functional environments, managing multiple priorities and recurring deadlines with incomplete or evolving information.
You are authorized to work in the United States. Please note that at this time, Everlaw is not sponsoring U.S. employment visas for this role.
Bonus points
Experience with ARR or ARRR reporting, SaaS metrics, or revenue recognition concepts.
Familiarity with financial planning tools (e.g., Adaptive Planning), ERPs (NetSuite), CRMs (Salesforce), or BI and data warehouse platforms (Looker, Tableau, Snowflake).
Working knowledge of SQL or data-querying tools.

The Finance team helps steward a strong business through its next stage of sustainable growth. Across accounting, planning, forecasting, reporting, procurement, controls, and financial systems, the team turns complex information into clear insights, dependable processes, and disciplined decisions. This work gives Everlaw the structure and confidence to invest thoughtfully, manage its resources responsibly, and scale without compromising what makes the company special.

When a lawsuit or investigation happens, teams must comb through vast amounts of electronic evidence — emails, documents, chats, files — to find what matters. title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
The Card Loan Platform team builds the high-throughput decision engine at the heart of Affirm’s card products. Unlike traditional cards, every pay-later transaction is backed by its own unique loan, and our system is the "invisible piping" that makes this complex model work at scale. Every swipe triggers our platform to solve a hard problem in milliseconds: matching messy, fragmented payment network data to the correct loan to drive real-time approvals, origination, and refunds.
As Affirm experiences explosive growth, our team's contributions are a key enabler. This isn't just another backend role; you'll be building the "financial brain" for our flagship card products, with your work on the critical path for every single swipe. We're tackling a unique, high-stakes distributed systems challenge that demands exceptional correctness and massive scale. You will partner closely with product, data science, and engineering teams to design and build the future of our industry-leading money movement platform.
If you are passionate about making foundational design decisions and building a beloved, lasting financial brand—come join us. It’s going to be an amazing ride!
What you'll do
Drive technical strategy by leading the planning, prioritization, and execution of projects, ensuring alignment with product, technical, and business goals.
Lead the end-to-end system design and development of large-scale, high-availability services. This includes building robust APIs and data models for our micro-service and event-driven architectures.
Collaborate across functions with partners in Product, Analytics, Design, Legal, and Accounting and to define requirements and execute our card loan attribution and lifecycle strategy.
Ensure system health and performance by analyzing and troubleshooting complex technical issues, optimizing existing code, and driving solutions that focus on long-term robustness and scalability.
Mentor and grow the team by guiding junior engineers, leading technical discussions and design reviews, and championing best practices through code review.
What we look for
5+ years of experience in software development or engineering, with a deep understanding of system design and architecture.
Motivated leader, inspiring team growth and fostering a culture of continuous learning
Excellent communicator, adept at sharing complex ideas with diverse audiences.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a creative and solution-oriented mindset.
Proficiency in modern programming languages such as Python, Kotlin, or similar.
Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes).
Knowledge of database systems (SQL, NoSQL), web frameworks, and RESTful API development.
This position requires either equivalent practical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in a related field.

title: Manager of Mortgage Sales
description:
About Homeward
Homeward takes the “what ifs” out of homebuying by creating financial products that give buyers and sellers certainty and convenience. We’re a fast-paced, remote-first real estate startup that partners with real estate agents to offer innovative products and services, helping clients buy with cash, sell with certainty, and time their move, regardless of the market.
Founder and CEO Tim Heyl, owner of one of the fastest-growing agent teams in the country, started Homeward in 2018 to fix the antiquated and broken real estate process. Today, we offer bundled cash offers, mortgage, and title services in 13 states, enabling buyers and sellers to move with certainty and convenience.
We’re a fully remote company with a diverse team spread across several countries - Grounded in three core values: The Golden Rule, One Team One Dream, and Calm Focus.
Hear from our employees about what our values mean to them
.
About the opportunity
Homeward Mortgage is hiring a Manager of Mortgage Sales to lead a small, high-producing team of Loan Officers and help us continue building a differentiated mortgage experience for Homeward’s buyers and agents.
Our Loan Officers operate in a high-volume environment, and this leader will be responsible for setting them up to consistently perform at an exceptional level. That means establishing clear expectations, holding the team accountable, coaching sales performance, and creating an environment where every Loan Officer takes ownership of every opportunity.
This is a highly hands-on leadership role. We are looking for someone who is willing to get into the weeds when a deal becomes difficult, whether that means digging into agency or investor guidelines, helping structure a complex scenario, coaching an agent conversation, or partnering with Operations to overcome an obstacle.
The right person is a strong sales leader with deep mortgage guideline knowledge who can solve problems, improve how the team operates, and knows when to coach the team versus when to jump in and help get a deal across the finish line.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.
In this role, you will:
Lead, coach, and develop a small team of high-producing Loan Officers, creating the structure and support they need to successfully manage high volume.
Monitor team and individual KPIs and SLAs, identify performance gaps, and translate data into specific coaching and action plans.
Foster a culture where every viable opportunity matters. Strong lead volume should never create complacency; we expect our team to fight for every customer and every deal.
Develop and maintain deep expertise in conventional, FHA, VA, investor, and Homeward-specific lending guidelines, becoming a trusted escalation point for complex scenarios.
Coach Loan Officers on sales conversations, objection handling, follow-up strategy, agent communication, and effective pipeline prioritization.
Develop Loan Officers who build strong agent relationships and become trusted financing partners to Homeward’s agent network.
Step into customer and agent escalations when leadership involvement can help protect the relationship, transaction, or customer experience.
Build a strong Sales and Operations partnership grounded in shared accountability. Hold the Sales team responsible for strong file quality and execution to mitigate preventable issues to move downstream.
Partner with Mortgage leadership and broader Homeward teams as we develop and improve unique Homeward mortgage products and offerings.
Facilitate regular team meetings and 1:1s that are actionable, performance-focused, and valuable to the Loan Officer team.
Foster a competitive but highly collaborative team environment aligned with Homeward’s Values and Culture.
Operate comfortably in a lean, fast-moving environment where leaders are expected to be resourceful, make sound decisions, and help build solutions..
What you’ll bring:
5+ years of residential mortgage experience, including direct experience originating purchase loans.
2+ years of experience leading, coaching, or managing Loan Officers in a high-production sales environment.
Deep working knowledge of conventional, FHA,  VA, and NonQM guidelines, with a demonstrated ability to research, interpret, and apply agency and investor requirements to complex borrower scenarios.
Proven experience leading a team to meet or exceed sales and conversion goals.
A customer- and agent-first mindset with high standards for communication, urgency, and follow-through.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to use performance data to identify opportunities and drive action.
Excellent judgment and the ability to balance sales urgency, customer advocacy, credit risk, and compliance requirements.
Strong cross-functional partnership skills and the ability to build productive relationships with Operations, Underwriting, Secondary, Compliance, Product, and senior leadership.
Comfort operating in an environment where not everything has already been built and where leaders are expected to help create the solution.
Strong ownership, high standards, and a bias toward action.
A genuine desire to set your team up for success and make the people around you better.
The drive to help build differentiated mortgage solutions that improve the real estate experience for Homeward’s customers and agents.
Compensation & Benefits
Compensation:
$75K base salary + $75K in variable compensation
Equity grant – stock options with real upside potential.
Benefits:
Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance coverage – with company contributions towards premiums.
Meaningful time off – including 20 days of paid vacation, 5 sick days, 12 company holidays, and 2 floating holidays.
Generous paid parental leave of up to 13 weeks.
401(k) with employer contribution match.
Remote-first work environment (our headquarters are in Austin, TX).
Collaborative, low-ego team that values intellectual curiosity and continuous improvement.
See more about how Homeward takes care of our team
here
.
Value-Driven Employee Experience
THE GOLDEN RULE
. It’s simple: Treat others the way we want to be treated. Whether we’re dealing with colleagues or customers, we don’t prioritize money or growth over people, and we practice empathy at every opportunity.
CALM FOCUS
. We work in tech and build solutions for real estate. Both are fast-paced and stressful industries. But by focusing on the larger objective rather than rushing from one task to the next, we can create solutions our customers love.
ONE TEAM, ONE DREAM
. Big problems require big solutions. We look at our customers’ experiences holistically and recognize that solving them requires collaboration across teams and our three affiliate companies — Homeward, Homeward Mortgage and Homeward Title.

title: Senior Software Engineer Guest & Host
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Guest & Host Technology builds the end-to-end experience that connects people around the world. Our team owns the identity and privacy layer beneath that experience: the systems that determine who can see what about whom, in what context, and why. That includes migrating how the rest of the company references users (moving from raw, global user identifiers to relationship-scoped identity), and building the privacy controls behind features like trip sharing and profile visibility. Get this layer wrong and it either breaks trust or breaks the product; our job is to make sure it does neither.
The Difference You Will Make:
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build and scale the backend systems behind user identity and privacy. You'll be reasoning about relationship-scoped access (who's allowed to see this, given the specific context they're asking from), and building systems that other teams across the company depend on to do the same correctly.
You'll work across true backend fundamentals: service architecture, data modeling, authorization logic, and migration tooling that needs to run safely at Airbnb's scale without breaking the dozens of teams who consume these systems.
A Typical Day:
Design and build backend services and APIs that enforce identity and privacy rules consistently across the company's product surfaces
Contribute to large-scale migrations (e.g., moving service and client code off legacy identity patterns) — including the tooling that makes those migrations safe to run broadly, not just the one-off fixes
Define and evolve authorization logic for context-scoped data access, and reason clearly about edge cases (e.g., who's allowed to see what, and why that answer differs by relationship or product surface)
Partner with the teams building on top of your systems — messaging, trips, profile, and beyond — to make sure privacy primitives are usable and hard to misuse
Participate in design and code reviews, and raise the bar for correctness on a part of the codebase where mistakes are costly
Debug and resolve production issues with clear, structured root-cause analysis rather than surface-level fixes
Your Expertise:
6+ years of professional backend software engineering experience, with strong fundamentals in service-oriented architecture, API design, and data modeling
Proficiency in Java and/or Kotlin, and comfort working within a microservices environment (RPC frameworks, service IDLs, dependency injection)
Experience designing systems with correctness and authorization as first-class concerns, not an afterthought
A track record of shipping migrations or infrastructure changes that other teams depend on, with attention to backward compatibility and rollout safety
Strong written communication. You can clearly document a problem, its root cause, and trade-offs between solutions before escalating or proposing a fix
Comfort with ambiguity: you can take a complex, evolving privacy or identity requirement and turn it into a concrete technical design without needing every detail spelled out
Your Location:

This role requires prior experience scaling compensation functions at high-growth or newly public technology companies. A flexible, growth mindset, comfort with ambiguity and change, and successfully balancing operational excellence with a sense of urgency will be critical to success in the role.

Strategy.
Define AlphaSense's multi-year compensation roadmap in alignment with market positioning that scales with the business. Own and manage the global compensation philosophy.
Structural Design.
Own and manage the global compensation structure across base, short-term incentives, and long-term incentives (equity), in alignment with job architecture.
Program Management.

Executive Compensation.

Advisory.
Partner with People Business Partners, business leaders, and managers to design compelling, scalable compensation solutions by seeking to understand the desired outcome, sharing market expertise, and proposing solutions. Provide guidance on complex, high-visibility compensation matters.
Market Intelligence.
Conduct quarterly and ad-hoc analyses to ensure external competitiveness, internal equity, and legal/pay-transparency compliance. Monitor market trends and ensure survey participation is completed to maximize our available benchmarking data set (e.g., Radford, Compa).
Education & Communication.

Governance.

title: Vice President, Marketing
description:
About Loyal
Loyal is a clinical-stage veterinary medicine company developing longevity drugs for dogs. Our mission is to help dogs live longer, healthier lives.
We're pioneering a new category of veterinary prescription drugs that proactively and preventatively target the underlying drivers of aging, delaying the onset of disease and preserving quality of life as dogs age. We've already made significant progress in our mission to develop the first FDA-approved drugs to extend canine lifespan: as of early 2026 we've completed two of three major FDA review sections for our lead program, LOY-002, and are targeting submission of the third and final section later this year.
Loyal is a
well-funded startup
with teams of scientists, veterinarians, engineers, operators, and creatives. You'll help us continue on our path of earning FDA approval for the first lifespan extension medicine for any species, and change what's possible for the dogs we love.
About the role
We’re seeking an experienced Vice President of Marketing to build out our consumer and vet marketing capabilities in preparation for the anticipated launch of our lead drug, LOY-002. This is a unique opportunity to set the strategy for how we will bring the first longevity drug for dogs to market.
You will own our marketing and communications plan end to end. This includes how we build an entirely new category of medicine, who we reach, how we reach them, what we say, and how we show up in the world.
The problem you’d be solving
We’re creating a category of medicine that doesn’t yet exist for two diverse audiences; veterinary professionals and consumers. While we’re in the pre-approval phase, this category creation work is essential to ensuring we have a strong foundation of vet professionals who understand our approach to targeting aging directly and trust the rigor and approaches our scientific, clinical, and manufacturing teams are taking. Just as important, this includes driving consumer awareness and understanding around aging as a treatable condition that dog owners should be looking to address directly.
Near-term this role is focused on building the category with both audiences. This includes early messaging and positioning work for aging care, honing our key audiences and how best to reach them, and building concrete plans for launch. It also means defining how we measure success in this pre-approval phase.
As we get closer to our anticipated launch (dependent on progress with the FDA) this role will evolve into team building and preparation for launch. This will include ensuring we have what we need in place to educate veterinary professionals, drive consumer demand, and continue to grow awareness of Loyal more broadly.
Company communications
Beyond launch preparations, you will also own how Loyal communicates as a company. We have a robust R&D pipeline and are looking for a leader who can set the strategy for what we talk about, when, why, and how. This includes communicating progress across all drugs in our pipeline, promoting key publications and partnerships, and situating Loyal in the center of longevity and senior dog care conversations.
What we’re looking for
This role is for someone who is a builder, can set strategy with an executive team while managing daily marketing tactics, and has strong taste and opinions for how to build a brand that is credible and trustworthy with veterinary professionals yet warm and accessible to consumers.
The ideal candidate should have a diverse marketing background across both consumers and professionals (healthcare/animal health a plus), be able to execute (not just direct), have a demonstrated track record of successful launches, and be a strong team leader and builder.
You will be reporting to our VP of Commercial and inherit our marketing team of two.
About you
You've built a marketing function from the ground up.
You've marketed to both consumers and professionals. Healthcare or animal health experience is a plus.
You've taken a product to market and you can talk specifically about what you'd do differently next time.
You have real taste and strong opinions about brand. Particularly how to be credible and rigorous with veterinary professionals while staying warm and accessible to consumers.
You're comfortable setting strategy with an executive team and working the tactics
You've hired and developed marketers
You can operate without a scoreboard while you define key metrics
Bonus, not required
You've marketed in a regulated category
You've built something people talked about without a large paid budget behind it
Salary Range: $275,000 - $335,000
Loyal benefits
Full-coverage health insurance — medical, dental and vision — for you and your dependents
$1,000 home office equipment stipend
$1,200/year learning budget for books, courses, etc.
$250/month wellness budget for gym, cleaners, spa, food, etc.
All 3-day weekends are turned into 4-day weekends 🎉
Unlimited vacation and paid holidays
Paw-ternity leave — adopt a dog and get a day off with your new family member 🐶
Competitive salary
Company equity options grant for new hires
Loyal is founded and led by a first-gen female CEO and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate against applicants based on gender, race or color, ethnicity or national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other applicable characteristics protected by law.
Our values
Moonshots, derisked methodically
Bringing the first longevity drug to market is an extremely difficult technical and social pursuit. To achieve this we must take bigger bets than the field has historically made, paired with the technical rigor to de-risk them step by step. We plan on both short and extremely long timescales, and we have the conviction to see our vision through to success or failure.
Opportunity is at the intersection
We lean into combining disciplines, expertise, and perspectives not normally adjacent. We design our organization to facilitate cross-pollination and cross-collaboration. We reject silos.
Expertise without ego
Titles do not determine who has a voice. We push back on each other, ask questions instead of issuing orders, and try to prove ourselves wrong. We are emotionally attached to the outcome, not our personal hypotheses, and welcome being challenged instead of treating it as a threat.
High agency, high humility
Most of what we're doing has never been done before, so we can't rely on established precedents to guide our way. We move forward to generate clarity, build strategies resilient to the fact that we don't know what we don't know, and design small experiments where we can fail safely, without jeopardizing the bigger mission.
Lead with transparency and context
We proactively and consistently share the why behind our strategy - not just the what - because we believe sharing context enables great people to make great decisions.
Empathy and respect for all life
Our patients are not just numbers. We deeply respect the value of every life, large and small and take our ethical responsibility to the families we treat extremely seriously.

Demonstrated experience in post approval regulatory activities is required.
This role requires both strategic vision and operational execution. The successful candidate will build and lead a regulatory organization capable of supporting Loyal across all stages of development and into a commercial company, and will serve as the primary regulatory authority and the company's primary interface with regulatory agencies globally.
The role reports to senior executive leadership and partners closely with leadership across TechOps, Quality, Clinical, Operations, and Commercial.
Your daily work will include
Own and drive Loyal's overall regulatory strategy across all active programs, including integrated CMC and clinical regulatory plans aligned with development milestones and commercial objectives, from early development through approval and post approval lifecycle management.
Provide regulatory input into portfolio planning, program prioritization, and business development activities, ensuring regulatory feasibility and risk are embedded in key decisions.
Develop and maintain global regulatory intelligence capabilities, monitoring evolving agency expectations, guidance documents, and industry precedents relevant to Loyal's programs and translating these into actionable strategy.
Provide regular regulatory updates and risk assessments to executive leadership and the board on submission progress, agency interactions, and regulatory risk.
Lead all CMC regulatory activities including filing strategy, CMC section authorship and review, post approval CMC change management, and regulatory oversight of manufacturing and CDMO partners.
Ensure CMC regulatory strategy reflects current agency expectations for small molecule OSD products and is integrated with CMC development plans and manufacturing timelines.
Partner with CMC and Quality leadership on CDMO regulatory readiness, including preparation for pre approval inspections and CMC related agency interactions.
Lead clinical regulatory activities including IND strategy and management, protocol regulatory review, study report oversight, and integration of clinical data into regulatory submissions.
Oversee regulatory strategy for pivotal studies and ensure alignment between study design, endpoints, and agency expectations to support a strong approval package.
Own the approval submission strategy and execution, coordinating across CMC, Clinical, and Quality to ensure submission ready packages that reflect current agency expectations and eCTD standards.
Serve as the company's primary liaison with regulatory agencies globally, leading the planning and execution of pre submission meetings, formal submissions, and ongoing agency communications.
Manage post approval regulatory obligations including periodic reports, labeling updates, post approval study commitments, and CMC variation filings, ensuring ongoing compliance with approval conditions.
Own labeling strategy and content development across the product lifecycle, ensuring labeling reflects agency requirements, clinical data, and commercial considerations, and is maintained in compliance with post approval obligations.
Establish and own Loyal's regulatory information management infrastructure, eCTD publishing capability, and submission archiving standards.
Build and lead a high performing regulatory organization, establishing clear functional ownership across CMC regulatory, clinical regulatory, submissions management, labeling, and regulatory operations.
Establish and scale regulatory governance frameworks and regulatory procedural documents — including submission templates, agency meeting management procedures, labeling review workflows, and regulatory decision documentation standards — that meet eCTD and global filing requirements and scale with the organization's growth.
Serve as the company's independent regulatory authority, with clear accountability to escalate regulatory risks, flag compliance concerns, and advise on activities where regulatory risk warrants executive attention.
Foster a culture of regulatory excellence and proactive risk management across the organization.
About you

title: Senior Mechanical Design Engineer – Liquid Cooling Systems
description:
About the Company
Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense.

We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.
Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.
About the role
Armada is seeking a
Senior Mechanical Systems / Design Engineer
to lead the design and development of liquid cooling and mechanical distribution systems for our modular AI data center platforms.
This role sits at the intersection of mechanical design, hydraulic engineering, thermal infrastructure, manufacturing, controls, and commissioning.
You will own the mechanical distribution architecture connecting heat-rejection equipment, pumps, piping, manifolds, coolant distribution units, rack cooling systems, and modular interconnects. You will translate system requirements into practical, serviceable, and repeatable designs that can be manufactured in a factory and deployed consistently across multiple sites.
This is not a traditional consulting or drawing-review role. You will help establish the design rules, technical standards, interfaces, and commissioning philosophy behind the product itself.
Location.
T
his role is remote.
What You'll Do (Key Responsibilities)
Mechanical and Liquid Cooling Architecture
Own the end-to-end mechanical cooling and fluid-distribution architecture for modular data center platforms.
Define primary, secondary, and rack-level cooling boundaries.
Establish pumping, flow-control, pressure-management, balancing, and redundancy strategies.
Align heat-rejection equipment, distribution piping, CDUs, rack manifolds, rear-door heat exchangers, and other cooling interfaces.
Develop scalable architectures that support multiple product configurations and deployment sizes.
Hydraulic System Design
Perform and review pipe-sizing, flow, pressure-drop, pump-head, and system-volume calculations.
Develop hydraulic models for water and glycol-based systems.
Account for fluid concentration, viscosity, temperature, fittings, valves, strainers, heat exchangers, and equipment pressure losses.
Define control-valve, balancing-valve, bypass, minimum-flow, and differential-pressure strategies.
Validate system performance across normal, part-load, maintenance, startup, and failure conditions.
Mechanical Design and Documentation
Own P&IDs, mechanical schematics, equipment schedules, valve schedules, instrumentation schedules, and design calculations.
Develop mechanical design criteria, basis-of-design requirements, and standard details.
Define clear equipment and scope boundaries between plant systems, modules, CDUs, rack cooling, and field interconnections.
Maintain disciplined revision control and technical traceability across the mechanical design package.
Review vendor drawings, submittals, calculations, and equipment selections for compliance with system intent.
Modular Product Integration
Define mechanical interfaces between factory-built modules and field-installed infrastructure.
Develop repeatable interconnect strategies for supply and return piping, manifolds, flexible connections, isolation valves, quick disconnects, drains, vents, and leak detection.
Establish labeling, connection, access, and installation standards that reduce field variability.
Support product configurations designed for transport, rapid installation, and phased expansion.
Design for Manufacturing and Serviceability
Develop layouts that support repeatable fabrication, assembly, inspection, testing, and installation.
Standardize piping routes, fittings, valve assemblies, supports, connection points, and mechanical components where practical.
Coordinate equipment clearances, removal paths, service access, drain points, vent points, and filter or strainer access.
Partner with manufacturing teams to resolve buildability issues and improve future revisions.
Translate field and factory feedback into product improvements.
Controls and Instrumentation Integration
Define the mechanical measurement and control requirements for temperature, flow, differential pressure, pressure, leak detection, fluid level, pump status, and valve position.
Partner with controls engineers to develop system operating sequences and alarm strategies.
Support pump staging, variable-speed control, minimum-flow protection, equipment enablement, and failure-response logic.
Help ensure mechanical system data is available for commissioning, operations, and remote monitoring.

Design systems for safe and efficient filling, flushing, venting, draining, testing, balancing, and startup.
Define isolation, bypass, temporary connection, and load-bank testing requirements.
Develop or support factory acceptance, site acceptance, and integrated systems testing procedures.
Establish performance-verification criteria for flow, pressure, temperature, heat rejection, controls, alarms, and failure modes.
Work directly with commissioning and field teams during startup and troubleshooting.
Cross-Functional Engineering Leadership
Partner with thermal, electrical, controls, structural, manufacturing, commissioning, supply chain, and product teams.
Coordinate directly with OEMs, equipment manufacturers, fabricators, and engineering partners.
Identify interface risks, design gaps, and single points of failure early.
Make clear technical decisions while maintaining alignment across the broader product architecture.
Communicate complex system behavior in a practical way to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

7 or more years of experience designing mechanical cooling, hydraulic distribution, process cooling, or mission-critical infrastructure systems.
Experience with data centers, semiconductor facilities, industrial process cooling, central utility plants, or comparable high-reliability environments.
Strong knowledge of pipe sizing, pump selection, pressure-drop analysis, flow balancing, system volume, and hydraulic control.
Experience developing and owning P&IDs, mechanical calculations, equipment schedules, valve schedules, and instrumentation requirements.
Practical knowledge of chilled-water, condenser-water, glycol, or process-fluid systems.
Experience designing for commissioning, maintenance, isolation, flushing, venting, draining, and service access.
Ability to coordinate across engineering, manufacturing, controls, commissioning, and field teams.
Strong technical judgment and the ability to own work with limited oversight.

Background in modular, prefabricated, skid-based, or containerized infrastructure.

Professional Engineer license or equivalent technical depth.

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Job Description:
B12's engineering team views software as a craft, but improving the world as the reason to practice it. Our engineers are responsible for prioritizing, conceptualizing, co-designing, building, testing, and engaging users for any concept we are building out. We’re generalists in encouraging each other to experience the full stack, but we’re also aware of each other’s preferences in the stack. For this role in particular, we’re searching for a tenured full-stack engineer who brings strong backend/infrastructure skills (and an interest in using them) to the product. We mentor and teach where we can, both inside and outside of the company, and as a Staff Software Engineer, you will be responsible not only for your ownership of major projects, but also mentorship of the team members with whom you ship those projects.
We value sharing our work with the outside world. Our team has
published papers
on forming expert flash teams and machine-mediated worker hierarchies. We’ve baked our research into various open source tools in the space of creativity, expertise, and knowledge work.
We hope our engineers have more longevity than any one tool we use, but here is a sampling of our current thoughts about technology:
We live on Python/Django and TypeScript/React.
We store blobs in Amazon’s S3, munch on them in Amazon’s EC2, develop in Docker, and deploy containers to Amazon’s Elastic Beanstalk.
We believe PostgreSQL should be the first system you consider when thinking about persisting structured data.
We clean and centralize data in Amazon’s Redshift, and are able to answer almost any question in SQL.
We leverage AI in our product and our internal tooling, and faced with a landscape in constant flux, try to pick the right model or agent on a task-by-task basis.
Our new code is almost 100% LLM-generated, and we’ve thought hard about
ensuring quality in the face of ever-increasing review loads
,
what processes humans are still best a
t, and
how the practice of mentorship must adapt in the face of these new tools
.
We have near-full test coverage on the backend, and are making progress on our frontend and integration tests.
We set up continuous integration and deployment because, while this model comes with its own pains, we’ve disliked being on fixed release schedules on previous projects.
We like to move fast and support point-in-time recovery :).
You’d be a good fit if
You have 10 or more years of experience building products and systems in production.
You are an amazing communicator.
You feel comfortable managing your time and deciding among competing priorities.
You are curious.
You have a high ownership mentality.
You enjoy learning and teaching.
You are comfortable working with backend and frontend technologies, but have a deeper background and interest on the backend/infrastructure side.
You care about and want to contribute to our mission of helping people do meaningful work.
What does a staff engineer do here?
This is B12’s first Staff Engineer hire on a ~10-person product team that includes a designer, product manager, and CTO. To understand what we’re looking for in someone with this much experience, here are some concrete examples of tasks you’d work on in a month:
Own the delivery of a project of the magnitude “we ship one or two of these a quarter,” both individually shipping code and rallying and supporting team members in doing so.
Participate in quarterly planning to identify key projects to work on next quarter.
Mentor other engineers who are in the planning, prototyping, or implementation phases of a project.
Respond to an incident, write up a postmortem, and improve tooling and infrastructure to help us prevent or more quickly respond to the issue and others like it in the future.
Identify and optimize some infrastructure that costs too much, is too slow, or isn’t stable enough.
Discuss an early design/prototype with a designer or product manager to help shape its direction and explain what will be easy or hard to implement.
Unblock an operational team member on a data analysis project that answers a hairy question facing our business.
Run a brainstorm with engineers to identify how we might work more effectively or ship with a higher level of quality.
Don’t fear:
We highly favor talent and interest.
Some candidates may see this list and feel discouraged because they don’t match all the items. Please apply anyway: there’s a good chance you’re more wonderful than you think you are.
B12 is a safe place for human beings. We particularly encourage you to apply if you identify as a woman, are a person of color or other underrepresented minority, or are a member of the LGBTQIA community.

title: Senior Clinical Implementation Manager (East)
description:
Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care. For Life Sciences partners, we offer the leading at-home EEG platform for clinical development of novel therapeutics for neurological, psychiatric, and sleep disorders. Our Diagnostics business is building the most comprehensive at-home platform for precision diagnostics, combining EEG and cardiopulmonary signals to deliver reimbursable assessments for sleep and central nervous system disorders. Together, we're changing the way patients are diagnosed and treated for any disorder that affects brain physiology.
What You Will Be Doing:
You will join Beacon's Clinical Implementation team, reporting to the National Clinical Implementation Director. This is a remote, US-based individual contributor role anchored in our East territory, with travel to customer sites across your assigned region. The role does not carry direct reports, but you will mentor peers and newer specialists and may direct the work of others on implementation projects.
You will own the clinical and operational implementation of Beacon's diagnostic solutions for assigned customers, guiding sleep labs, health systems, and provider organizations from contract pre-signature through confident, sustained daily use of our products. Day to day, that means delivering demos, building implementation plans, running clinical education and training, supporting go-lives, and coaching accounts through adoption after launch.
This is not a traditional implementation role focused only on deployment and go-live milestones. Your impact is measured by sustained usage, behavioral adoption, and long-term workflow integration. At this level, your influence extends beyond your own accounts: you set the standards, playbooks, and best practices the broader team works from, and you help shape where the clinical implementation function goes over the next several quarters.
The role is highly cross-functional and requires strong communication, systems thinking, empathy, and execution discipline. You will work across clinicians, executives, and frontline staff while maintaining clarity, momentum, and trust throughout the customer journey.
Beacon's robust asynchronous work practices ensure a first-class remote work experience, but we also have in-person office hubs available located in Boston, New York, or the Bay Area.
What Success Looks Like:
You own end-to-end implementation execution for your accounts such as kickoff, project planning, milestone tracking, risk identification, and stabilization, and the accounts transition cleanly into steady-state support with decisions and configurations documented.
You provide virtual and on-site clinical support across every phase of implementation, from pre-planning and education through go-live and post-launch troubleshooting.
You build implementation plans that account for clinical workflow design, staffing models, order and result routing, patient communication, and administrative processes, and you coordinate resources across Customer Success, Clinical, Technical Services, Support, and Product to keep them on schedule.
You deliver comprehensive training and demos tailored to each audience (physicians, advanced practice providers, sleep technologists, medical assistants, schedulers, and administrative staff) and maintain the reusable materials, quick-reference guides, and competency checklists that make training repeatable.
You own adoption outcomes, tracking utilization, ordering patterns, turnaround, and workflow adherence against agreed targets, and delivering refresher training as turnover, new hires, and product changes require.
You diagnose the root cause of low or inconsistent usage (workflow friction, training gaps, staffing constraints, process breakdown) in situations where the data alone does not give you the answer, and you drive corrective action.
You partner with clinical and operational leaders to redesign workflows so Beacon is embedded in daily practice, and you connect usage data back to the customer's stated clinical and operational goals.
You serve as the clinical operational point of contact through pre-sale, implementation, and early adoption, building trusted relationships from frontline staff to the executive level and communicating status, risks, and decisions proactively.
You act as the clinical subject matter expert on sleep testing workflows and home sleep apnea testing, ensuring clinical messaging and training content align with product capabilities, supporting evidence, and regulatory requirements.
You exercise independent judgment on methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria, including how implementations are sequenced, how adoption is measured, and what counts as a stabilized account, and you determine your own approach on first-of-kind customers, new indications, and accounts with no precedent.
You partner with Regional Sales Managers on clean handoffs, participate in QBRs and renewal or expansion discussions, and surface adoption risks, churn signals, and expansion opportunities early with supporting evidence.
You give Product structured feedback grounded in real implementation experience, identify recurring friction points, propose scalable solutions, and support go-to-market readiness for new features and indications.
You mentor and coach peers and newer specialists on strategy, execution, customer judgment, and collaboration, including areas outside their functional skillset, and you build the templates and playbooks that raise the team's standard.
You prioritize and plan multi-quarter priorities for the clinical implementation function, represent it in cross-team planning with Sales, Product, and Customer Success, and make decisions based on the needs of multiple stakeholder teams and the company as a whole.
You initiate improvement projects independently, arriving with a defensible approach rather than waiting for direction, where recurring gaps in process, tooling, or enablement limit team outcomes.
You adhere to all regulatory, compliance, quality, and privacy standards applicable to medical devices and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), including HIPAA, and support audits, documentation, and quality processes as required.
Must-Haves:
Active RPSGT certification
8+ years of direct experience in sleep medicine, sleep lab operations, or home sleep apnea testing
Demonstrated experience owning demos, customer implementations, clinical training, or go-live support in healthcare settings
Experience delivering training and education to both clinical and administrative audiences
Experience working cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Support, Marketing, and Product teams
Demonstrated experience mentoring or coaching peers, and setting standards or best practices adopted beyond your own work
Experience planning work across multiple quarters and multiple stakeholder groups
Willingness to travel nationally (up to ~50-75%), including on-site go-live support
Familiarity with CRM tools, enablement platforms, and project tracking tools
US-based, anchored in the East territory
Nice-to-Haves
Adoption-focused mindset.
You measure success by sustained usage, workflow integration, and customer outcomes rather than implementation completion alone.
Clinical workflow fluency.
You understand sleep lab workflows and how clinicians and their teams operate in practice, not just on paper.
Systems and operational thinking.
You see how implementation, training, adoption, workflow optimization, and customer success connect into a single operating system.
Independent judgment at scale.
Your recommendations are trusted without close oversight, and you are comfortable defining the approach when no playbook exists.
A multiplier effect.
You raise the performance of those around you through mentorship, reusable best practices, and standards that outlast any single implementation.
Comfort in a fast-paced environment.
You execute effectively in a high-growth startup where priorities evolve quickly.
Familiarity with CRM tools, enablement platforms, project tracking tools, and healthcare IT systems (EHR/EMR exposure a plus).
Experience supporting SaMD or regulated medical device products.
Prior experience at an early- or growth-stage healthcare company.
Experience building a function's playbooks, templates, or training curricula from the ground up.
The salary range for this role is $135,000 – $155,000. Salary ranges are determined using current market compensation data for this role and adjusted based on experience, skills, and location. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes equity, PTO and other benefits.
At Beacon, we've found that cultural and scientific impact is driven most by those that lead by example. As such, we're always seeking new contributors whose work demonstrates an avid curiosity, a bias towards simplicity, an eye for composability, a self-service mindset, and - most of all - a deep empathy towards colleagues, stakeholders, users, and patients. We believe a diverse team builds more robust systems and achieves higher impact.

Hire, develop, and keep great designers.

10+ years in design, with at least four leading a multidisciplinary in-house creative team, including managing Creative Directors or other people managers.
A portfolio with two kinds of receipts: work you made, and work your team made under your direction. Brand and campaign work with a clear point of view.
Experience building and governing a brand design system in a fast-moving company, and keeping it in use.
Hands-on experience bringing AI tools into a creative team's workflow, with a real opinion on where they help, where they don't, and how you protect quality along the way.
Experience producing video and motion for marketing, either directly or by building the team and vendor mix to do it.
Experience running agencies, contractors, and a budget from RFP through delivery.
Comfort represents design to C-level partners, making the case for creative quality with clarity and data, and saying no when the work doesn't meet the bar.
Craft depth across Adobe Creative Cloud, Figma, motion and video tools like After Effects and Premiere, and AI-assisted workflows. Enough to evaluate and lift the team's work, and to contribute when needed.
Bonus points if
you've led design through a brand transformation, shaped how AI features get expressed visually in a product people trust with their money, partnered with web and growth teams on redesigns and conversion testing, or worked in fintech or another regulated industry.
What success looks like
BILL's brand looks distinctive, modern, and unmistakably ours across every channel, and the market notices.
The design team ships more, faster, with AI built into how the work gets made, and the craft is better, not worse.
Video is a standing capability with a pipeline, a cadence, and a body of work: social ads, product explainers, and launch films.
Brand, Web, and Demand gen partners describe the team as an enabler, not a bottleneck.
The team is innovative and growing. People want to work here. You’re shipping work that makes everyone at BILL proud of where they work.
How we work
We move fast, take real positions, and would rather ship fewer, sharper ideas than fill a calendar. We value clear thinking, direct feedback, and the willingness to say no to work that doesn't meet the bar.

title: Risk Analyst II
description:
Who is Boulevard?
Boulevard provides the first and only client experience platform for appointment-based, self-care businesses. We empower our customers to give their clients more of the magical moments that matter most.
Before launching in 2016, our founders spent months interviewing salon managers and working behind front desks to understand their pain points so we could design a modern, user-friendly platform that meets the unique needs of their business.
