Our technology not only helps our customers survive but thrive. Take a look at
how we (and YOU) can make that happen
.
We have an insatiable curiosity and embrace experimentation. We believe that simple solutions require the most sophistication, and we design each and every detail to maximize potential, power, and impact. Do our values match? Read through
our story and what we value the most
.
Our team values and celebrates our diverse backgrounds. Being open about who we are and what we do allows us to do the best work of our lives. We believe in equal opportunity for all, and you should too.
Come do the best work of your life at Boulevard.
Integrated payments processing is a core component of Boulevard’s industry-leading business management platform. Processing over $3B annually and growing fast, we have ambitious goals for our payments business and are looking for a Risk Analyst to help review and approve merchant applications, monitor customer transactions for potential risk, and handle payments-related customer escalations.
The Risk Analyst II conducts the reviews of new merchants as they are onboarded to ensure compliance with our internal policies, our processors guidelines, card brand rules as well as federal regulations. They also make recommendations for enhancements that will streamline the underwriting process and improve the merchant experience.
What you’ll do here
Conduct comprehensive merchant application reviews
and analyses, covering Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-money laundering (AML) rules
Review and analyze flagged transactions
and other alerts,
making well-reasoned recommendations around compliance with payments processing standards
Assist in the development of fraud detection & risk management systems
and tools, suggesting enhancements as needed
Review merchant transaction history
to assess risk level and make approval recommendations for various payment processing limits
Manage inquiries and requests
from customers, partners, and internal teams
Collaborate with internal teams,
including Onboarding and Customer Support, and external partners on payment processing-related matters
What you’ll need to thrive:
High School Diploma minimum, Bachelor's degree preferred
3 - 7 years of experience in the payment industry, with a focus on underwriting, transaction monitoring, customer support and/or fraud/risk management
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Google, especially Excel/Sheets
Familiarity with merchant processing platforms and applications
Knowledge of card brands (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) rules and regulations
Awareness of PCI compliance
Ability to read and understand credit card processing statements
Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and research capabilities
Able to research and make decisions on complex merchant-related issues then relay findings
Comfortable reaching out to customers directly via email or phone calls to review merchant application details
Experience with SQL, Tableau or Sigma is a plus
Autonomous work ethic, comfortable in a digitally connected environment
How we'll take care of you:
At Boulevard, we work hard to structure compensation in a way that balances internal equity with local market competitiveness, and we’re happy to share a good-faith estimate of the base salary range for this role. For U.S. based candidates, the anticipated base salary range is $101,000 - $119,000 per year. In addition to this base compensation, this role may be eligible to participate in a variable compensation program. Final compensation will vary based on a variety of factors, which include but are not limited to, applicable experience, location, and final leveling.

Our business is deeply immersed in an industry that’s centered around helping people feel their best, so we know that taking care of yourself isn’t selfish; it’s essential. That’s why our culture pairs high standards with genuine care. We don't glorify burnout or wear ‘always on’ as a badge of honor. Instead, we’ve created benefits designed to support you inside and outside of work, so you can bring your best self to both.
Here’s how we support you:
Competitive base pay and performance bonus eligibility because you deserve to be rewarded for your impact.
Equity participation for all full-time employees because we believe the people helping build Boulevard should share in our long-term success.
Comprehensive medical coverage with up to 100% employee premium coverage and 75% dependent coverage to help take care of you and your loved ones.
An annual $1,200 HSA employer contribution for eligible plans to help support healthcare costs and future planning.
100% covered dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, ensuring you stay healthy, protected, and ready for whatever life brings.

This role marks Bubble’s deliberate move to bring strategy, execution, and accountability closer to the business.

Develop and execute an integrated paid media strategy across upper-funnel brand media, social, digital, and retailer media.
Own holistic paid media budget management, balancing investment between brand equity-building and performance-driving channels.
Manage and optimize media across  Walmart Connect, Target Roundel, Ulta.com, DTC and other
retailer.com
platforms. Partner with the Director of Amazon to deliver topline Amazon paid strategy, work with Amazon agency on execution and KPI delivery.
Develop retailer media strategies that amplify and extend Bubble’s broader brand campaigns, launches and cultural moments.
Partner with Brand Marketing to ensure paid media builds awareness among our core audience, relevance and consideration, while creating a clear path to conversion.

Collaborate with Creative and Brand Marketing to develop platform-native content and advertising that works across both brand and performance environments.
Lead ongoing testing of audiences, creative, messaging, placements, keywords and investment levels to continuously improve performance.
Provide clear insights and recommendations to leadership on how media investment is building both Bubble’s brand and the business.
Retail Media Networks
Lead strategy and execution across Walmart Connect, Target Roundel, Ulta UB Media, Criteo, and other RMNs - managing two distinct but connected workstreams: tent-pole campaign activations and always-on display and search.
Always-on media
- own the day-to-day management of retail.com display and sponsored search activity, including keyword bidding, bid optimization, audience targeting, and spend pacing. This is an active, hands-on workstream requiring regular monitoring and continuous efficiency improvements.
Campaign activations

Manage Bubble’s paid media mix for hellobubble.com across Meta, TikTok, Google Search, and YouTube - covering both prospecting and retargeting.
Build and optimize campaigns that balance customer acquisition efficiency (ROAS, CAC) with brand awareness.
Partner with the creative team to brief platform-specific content and run ongoing creative testing.
Stay current on emerging ad formats and proactively test new opportunities.

Partner with the Senior Director of Ecommerce on email and SMS strategy - sharing paid media insights to inform segmentation, offers, and creative testing.

Commercial & Marketing Teams

Partner with finance on spend forecasting and budget tracking.

6+ years of experience
in paid media, digital marketing, retail media or integrated media planning – brand or agency side.

Solid working knowledge of DTC paid channels: search, social, and retargeting.

title: Sr. Clinical Research Associate/Clinical trial Manager
description:
Mavericks Wanted
When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on
In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible.
Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. If you're someone who defies convention, join us and work alongside some of the most respected minds in the industry. Together, we'll ask "why not?" and help reengineer the future of biopharma. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical & thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work.
Company Overview
BridgeBio is a biopharmaceutical company founded to discover, create, test, and deliver transformative medicines for patients with genetic diseases and cancers with clear genetic drivers. Founded in 2015, the company has built a portfolio of 20+ drug development programs spanning preclinical to late-stage development across multiple therapeutic areas.
QED Therapeutics, an affiliate of BridgeBio Pharma,
is dedicated to developing targeted treatments for FGFR-driven skeletal dysplasia, focusing on Achondroplasia (ACH) and Hypochondroplasia (HCH). Achondroplasia is the most common form of genetically driven short stature, and Hypochondroplasia is a genetic condition that affects the way bones grow; both conditions can lead to significant medical complications throughout life. With our investigational therapeutic candidate, infigratinib, we seek to deliver meaningful treatment options that address the underlying cause of these conditions and improve outcomes for children and families living with ACH and HCH.
What You’ll Do
As a Sr. Clinical Research Associate/Clinical Trial Manager, you will collaborate within the Clinical Operations team to support the timely conduct of clinical studies according to protocols, GCP, SOPs, and applicable regulations. You will be responsible for performing quality study oversight processes, including monitoring communications with site staff and clinical vendors, and reviewing monitoring trip reports.
Partner with the Clinical Operations Study Lead and cross-functional team to support clinical studies from planning and start-up through execution, maintenance, and close-out in accordance with assigned SOPs, ICH/GCP, and corporate and departmental goals.
Lead operational management for assigned regions and sites by driving site initiation activities, monitoring performance metrics, identifying and mitigating risks, driving escalations and action-item closure, and representing regional performance in study team and cross-functional discussions.
Lead aspects of vendor management for the CRO and other key vendors (IRT, imaging, central and specialty labs, etc.), establishing expectations, ensuring deliverables are met, performance measures are maintained, and escalating as needed; address performance gaps and drive corrective actions to closure.
Provide oversight of CRO monitors by reviewing monitoring documentation, evaluating monitor and site performance, conducting oversight or co-monitoring visits as needed, and identifying cross-site or systemic risks.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of study documents, including informed consent forms, site training materials, CRFs, monitoring plans, source document templates, protocols, investigator brochures, and regulatory submission materials under the direction of the study lead.
Ensure the Trial Master File is complete, current, accurate, and inspection-ready, and drive resolution of missing or deficient documentation.
Apply ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice principles, including quality by design, risk-proportionate oversight, critical-to-quality factors, participant protection, and reliable trial results, across study activities.
Exercises sound judgment to resolve or, as appropriate, seek expert input on protocol and drug questions, safety, regulatory, and legal questions.
Participates in the review and negotiation of site budgets and contracts.
Support and participate in Investigator Meetings and other study-related meetings, as required.
Promote a collaborative, respectful, quality-focused work environment.
Additional Clinical Operations activities may be assigned as appropriate.
Travel as required to carry out responsibilities (up to 20%).
Where You'll Work
This is a U.S.-based remote role that will require quarterly or as-needed visits to our San Francisco Office
.
Who You Are

title: Data Scientist II
description:
CareDx is a leading precision medicine diagnostics company advancing care in transplant, specialty oncology, and cell therapy. Through our innovative portfolio of molecular diagnostics, digital health solutions, AI-powered data and analytics, and patient support services, we partner with healthcare providers, patients, and biopharma organizations to help inform clinical decision-making and improve patient outcomes.
At CareDx, every employee has the opportunity to contribute to innovations that help transform patient care and improve lives.
The Data Scientist II will develop clinically grounded, interpretable AI and analytics solutions that support commercial, medical affairs, clinical research, and enterprise decision-making. The role will translate integrated structured and unstructured data into reliable insights, actionable recommendations, and reusable analytical products.
This role combines applied data science, statistical modeling, machine learning, generative AI, and research collaboration. The Data Scientist II will own defined workstreams from problem framing and research design through modeling, validation, documentation, deployment support, and stakeholder communication. Success requires strong quantitative judgment, reproducible development practices, and the ability to communicate methods, limitations, and recommendations clearly to technical, scientific, clinical, and business stakeholders.
Responsibilities
· Own analytics and AI workstreams for next-best-action and field education capabilities, translating integrated data into actionable recommendations.
· Advance literature intelligence workflows, including search, retrieval, synthesis, evaluation, and validation of AI-generated outputs.
· Develop interpretable machine learning, statistical, and generative AI solutions using structured and unstructured clinical, laboratory, commercial, and enterprise data.
· Build reproducible workflows and reusable components that can progress from research prototypes to reliable applications and decision-support tools.
· Lead analytics research proposals and collaborations, including cohort definition, analysis planning, modeling, interpretation, and communication of results.
· Partner with clinicians, scientists, medical affairs, research teams, and business stakeholders to translate questions into rigorous analytical plans and defensible results.
· Support abstracts, presentations, and research reports while applying appropriate privacy, security, validation, and documentation practices.
· Contribute to and provide backup support for forecasting, Promotion Effectiveness, and Digital Product Impact initiatives.
· Perform exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model development and evaluation, sensitivity testing, and scenario analysis using Python or R and SQL.
· Collaborate with data and application engineers on pipelines, version control, testing, deployment readiness, monitoring, and maintenance; clearly document data lineage, assumptions, limitations, and recommendations.
Qualifications
· Bachelor of Science (BS) or Master of Science (MS) degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Biostatistics, Bioinformatics, or a related quantitative field.
· 5+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, advanced analytics, AI engineering, or a related role, including 3+ years in healthcare, diagnostics, biotechnology, clinical research, life sciences, or another regulated environment.
· Strong hands-on proficiency in Python or R, SQL, and Git-based development workflows.
· Experience developing and validating predictive, descriptive, statistical, or machine learning models using real-world clinical, EHR, laboratory, research, or other complex longitudinal data.
· Ability to produce audit-ready documentation covering data lineage, methods, assumptions, testing, validation, and model limitations.
· Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate across technical, scientific, clinical, and business teams.
Preferred Qualifications
· Experience with AI-enabled search, natural language processing, literature intelligence, retrieval-augmented generation, or document synthesis.
· Experience moving analytical prototypes into user-facing or production workflows, including testing, monitoring, and ongoing support.
· Familiarity with Databricks, cloud data platforms, model lifecycle management, and modern analytics application frameworks.
· Experience contributing to clinical research deliverables such as protocols, abstracts, presentations, manuscripts, or analytical reports.
How We Work
Curiosity: Start with Why
We understand why a project matters, what problem we are solving, whom it helps, and what success looks like. We ask thoughtful questions, align early, and move forward with confidence.
Accountability: Extreme Ownership
We take responsibility for what we build and deliver. We communicate risks early, follow through on commitments, and help resolve problems rather than waiting for detailed direction.
Transparency: Default to Share
We proactively share context, decisions, progress, and lessons learned. We document and demonstrate our work so others can build on it.
Empowerment: Amplify Others
We succeed as a team. We collaborate openly, recognize the contributions of others, and give credit generously.
Resilience: Learn Loudly
We treat mistakes and unexpected outcomes as opportunities to improve. We focus on solutions, identify root causes, and share what we learn.

title: Staff Application & Product Security Engineer
description:
You will be the most senior hands-on application security engineer at Cleo, owning both how security is built into our products from design through release and the security posture of the products we ship, both
on-premise
and SaaS, as our customers experience them. This is a Staff-level individual contributor role with real program ownership: you set the standards, build the guardrails, and work directly with engineers in the code. You report to the CISO and partner daily with Engineering, and our Cloud Security team. You are not a one-person department: security engineers and consulting partners execute under your direction. Your job is to set direction, make the hard technical calls, and build leverage through automation and partners rather than carry every task yourself.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities
Secure development lifecycle and guardrails
Own and mature Cleo’s SSDLC: security requirements, threat modeling, and design reviews for high-risk product changes, APIs, and integrations.
Run and tune SAST, SCA, secrets detection, container, and IaC scanning.
Build reusable secure patterns, reference implementations, and policy-as-code controls that make the secure path the default path.
Own developer security enablement: Security Champions meeting, deliver the engineering security training campaigns, grow a named champion in every squad, and give developers practical remediation guidance, office hours, and self-service security capabilities.
Product vulnerability management
Run risk-based triage, remediation, and verification for application and product vulnerabilities, including remediation SLAs, escalation, and exceptions. Reproduce externally reported vulnerabilities against running product instances and validate patches before release.
Own the penetration testing program: scope and coordinate third-party engagements, perform targeted testing yourself, and validate findings through retesting.
Run our Vulnerability Disclosure Program, including researcher communications and coordinated disclosure.
Coordinate the CVE lifecycle for Cleo products and support product-security incident response.
Own the application and product-security controls in Cleo's NIST CSF 2.0 program: track maturity, close gaps, and produce the evidence our audits rely on.
Product security
Own the security posture of the products Cleo ships, across SaaS and customer-hosted deployment models: secure defaults, authentication and session controls, RBAC and tenant isolation, admin data access, security-relevant configuration, and hardening guidance for customers.
Own the Product Security Roadmap: partner with Product Management, the CTO, and Architecture to get security features prioritized and shipped, including SSO/SAML upgrades, the in-app RBAC redesign, endpoint-level access control, and customer-requested controls, and represent security in RTE Sync and Boundary Review.
Be the technical owner for customer-facing product security: triage customer vulnerability-scan findings and penetration-test reports against Cleo products, answer security RFIs and enhancement requests, and author customer-facing advisories, security release notes, and hardening documentation.
AI Fluency Competencies
Own threat modeling and security review for LLM-enabled product features, AI agents, and AI-assisted development workflows.
Build controls and secure patterns for prompt injection, sensitive data exposure, insecure output handling, excessive agency, insecure tool integrations, and AI supply-chain risk.
Apply and operationalize the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework across product and engineering.
Prerequisites
6+ years in application security, product security, or secure software engineering, including experience building or maturing an AppSec program across multiple engineering teams.
Strong object-oriented developer:
Strong proficiency in an object-oriented programming language is required, with Java preferred given Cleo’s core products are Java-based. You should be able to read, debug, and write production-quality code and be comfortable working across languages such as TypeScript, Python, or Go.
Deep knowledge of application attack surfaces: authentication, authorization, API security, business-logic flaws, and modern service architectures.
Hands-on experience integrating and tuning SAST, SCA, and secrets scanning in GitHub and CI/CD pipelines.
Hands-on exploit reproduction and patch validation: you can take a researcher's report of a pre-authentication vulnerability, reproduce it against a running Java web application, confirm the fix, and write up what the researcher and the customer each need to hear.
Coordinated disclosure experience with external security researchers and customers, including holding an embargo timeline and driving a CVE to publication.
Product security experience on shipped software with an installed base: secure defaults and hardening guidance, customer-facing advisories and security release notes, and turning a customer's scan report or RFI into a fix-or-explain response.
Experience running threat modeling, design reviews, and manual security testing, and working directly with developers through remediation.
Clear communicator who can turn technical risk into engineering guidance for both developers and executives, and who can hold a release-gating decision with Engineering leadership when the risk warrants it.
Nice to Have
Securing LLM applications, AI agents, or AI-assisted development tools.
SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX), VEX, artifact signing, and SLSA.
AWS, Kubernetes/EKS, Terraform, Jenkins.
Snyk, GitHub Advanced Security, Semgrep, Burp Suite.
NIST CSF 2.0, OWASP SAMM/ASVS, NIST SSDF; supporting SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audits.
CSSLP, OSWE, GWAPT, AWS Security, or comparable certifications.

title: Grant Writer
description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.
We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.
We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.
About the Role
Location:
Remote (US)
Role Type:
Full-Time Contractor (40 hours/week)
Duration:
9-month contract
Reports To:
Sr. Manager, Development Operations
Compensation:
$7,000–9,200 per month
This is not a traditional nonprofit grant writing role.
CodePath's Philanthropy Partnerships team raises the capital behind our courses, our career support, and our students' outcomes. The Grant Writer is how that case gets made. You write for national foundations and corporate partners deciding where their social impact dollars go, and you translate program data, student outcomes, and organizational strategy into the proposals and reports that win major commitments and steward them.
The second half of the job makes the first half repeatable. You partner with Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data to stay ahead of fast-moving program updates and impact metrics, then turn what you learn into reusable assets, writing frameworks, and AI-enabled workflows the whole team draws on.
CodePath is an AI-native organization, and we expect this role to work like one. Writing faster with AI is table stakes. We want someone who builds the systems that raise everyone's output — so the team spends its time on strategy and judgment instead of rebuilding the same narrative from scratch.
CodePath is scaling fast. This is the role that lets our fundraising capacity scale with it.
Key Activities
Proposal development (~20%)
Lead or support major grant proposals, concepts, and letters of inquiry from prospecting through submission, meeting every funder guideline and submission requirement
Translate CodePath's mission, programs, and impact into compelling, consistent narratives the whole team can use
Research, synthesize, and translate program data into funder-facing briefs, proposals, and supporting materials
Build the frameworks and narratives that equip account owners to lead complex, high-value opportunities
Grant reporting and compliance (~10%)
Serve as lead or supporting writer on major funder reports
Equip account owners with the narratives, data, and frameworks they need to lead complex funder reports and steward high-value relationships
Proactively manage funder portal accounts, submission calendars, and organizational credentials
Keep internal grant management systems (e.g., Asana) current
Asset development and maintenance (~20%)
Build and maintain a shared library of reusable narrative assets — program descriptions, boilerplate language, proof points — that accelerates every proposal the team writes
Support fundraisers with ad-hoc narrative development
Cross-functional collaboration (~20%)
In partnership with the Sr. Manager of Development Operations, collaborate with other departments (e.g., Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data) to collect and translate data, program updates, and student stories into funder-facing narratives
Supply narrative inputs, source content, program context, data, and proof points for donor-facing assets alongside fundraisers and the rest of the Philanthropy Partnerships team
Writing enablement and team optimization (~30%)
Use AI tools to improve how proposals, reports, and assets get built
Track fast-moving organizational developments and impact metrics to keep fundraising materials current and accurate
Develop and maintain proposal templates, writing frameworks, reusable assets, and funder-specific approaches that let account owners lead complex proposals and reports themselves
Document writing patterns and organizational knowledge to improve AI-assisted drafting and automate routine work, while holding quality, accuracy, and a consistent CodePath voice
Key Success Metrics
At 30 days
You understand CodePath's mission, program model, core narratives, impact data, and active funder portfolio
You know the team's proposal and reporting workflows, writing standards, and priorities
You have met the cross-functional teams and know where the information you need lives
At 60 days
You have contributed to active proposals or reports, turning existing CodePath information into clear, accurate funder-facing writing
You manage your assigned deliverables and deadlines, including funder requirements
You have added new or updated materials to the shared asset library
You have working relationships with key Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data counterparts
At 90 days
You write proposals and reports that come back with strategic refinements, not substantive rewrites
You run assigned deliverables independently from information gathering through submission
You navigate cross-functional relationships efficiently to get what you need
The shared library is stronger — easier for the team to find, adapt, and keep current
You have shipped at least two repeatable or AI-enabled workflows that cut manual effort or free the team for higher-value work
Account owners are leading their own proposals and reports on complex opportunities, using frameworks and synthesis you built
You are a trusted writing partner to the Philanthropy Partnerships team
Qualifications
Required
5–7 years writing for institutional and corporate funders
— proposals, letters of inquiry, and funder reports. Long-form, funder-facing, and written by you.
You build with AI, you don't just write with it.
You have documented recurring work, streamlined it with AI tools, and handed the result to other people. Using Claude or ChatGPT to polish a draft is not what we mean.
You do your own data synthesis.
You go to the data and finance teams, ask the right questions, and turn what you get back into accurate narrative — without waiting for someone to hand you a summary.
You collaborate across functions and come in curious.
You want to understand the programs and the strategy, not just the ask.
You work at pace.
Concurrent deadlines, shifting priorities, and information that changes under you.
Exceptional writing and editing, with attention to detail while maintaining a strategic perspective.
Preferred
Experience in education, workforce development, or youth-serving nonprofits
Experience in a social impact, tech, or tech-adjacent environment
CRM management, HubSpot preferred
Asana or similar project management platforms
Comfort building simple visual assets (e.g., Canva)

We are looking for a Full Stack Engineer to build the integrations that put Nametag inside the systems our customers already use.

Our reach is determined by how well we embed into Workday, ServiceNow, Slack, Okta, ICIMS, UKG, and the long tail behind them — and that embedding is engineering work.
This is a full stack role with an unusual center of gravity. You'll write backend services and APIs on our side, configuration and setup experiences in our console, and the connector code that talks to a dozen platforms that each made different decisions about authentication, extensibility, and what a webhook means. You'll join a dedicated team whose purpose is expanding Nametag into new systems and new use cases.
What makes this work interesting is that you're building into environments you don't control and can't change. Every target platform has its own auth model, its own rate limits, its own review process, and its own idea of how much UI you're allowed. Workday's extensibility surface is narrow and governed. Slack gives you modals and Block Kit, which were not designed for identity verification. ServiceNow gives you enough rope to break a customer's upgrade path. Designing something that is secure, usable, and actually buildable inside those limits — and that keeps working when the vendor ships a change you didn't ask for — is the core of the job.
The breadth is real. You'll be reading someone else's API documentation most weeks, and debugging behavior that documentation doesn't describe. Engineers who like going deep on one system for a year will be unhappy here. Engineers who like landing in an unfamiliar platform and having it figured out by Thursday will do well.
You'll work closely with the product manager for integrations, who owns how each integration should work, and you'll have real influence over that design because you're the one who knows what the platform will actually permit.

The Role
We are looking for a Full Stack Engineer to own the platform foundations everything else at Nametag is built on.
Most engineering roles here ship features. This one owns the substrate: the data model, the Postgres layer beneath it, the public APIs our customers build against, the multi-region architecture that lets us serve customers who cannot let data leave their jurisdiction, and the governance machinery that makes our claims about data handling true rather than aspirational.
That last part is not a compliance footnote. We hold government-issued identity documents, selfies, and biometric signals. Customers ask us exactly where that data lives, who can reach it, how long we keep it, and what happens when they ask us to delete it — and their auditors ask again, in writing. Retention and deletion have to actually execute, including in replicas, derived tables, caches, and backups, which is where most deletion guarantees quietly fail. Tenant isolation has to be enforced by the data layer, not by every query remembering to filter correctly. Building those guarantees into the platform, so that product engineers get them by default instead of having to be careful, is the central work of this role.
Multi-region is the other structural piece. Serving customers with data residency requirements means region-aware routing, storage, and failover, and a data model that knows which rows are allowed where. It's the kind of architecture that is much cheaper to get right early than to retrofit, and you'll be shaping it.
You'll also own our public API surface — design, versioning, deprecation, and the discipline of not breaking customers who integrated two years ago and have no plans to change.
This is a full stack role in the real sense: the center of gravity is backend and data, but you'll build the internal tooling, admin surfaces, and operational dashboards that make the platform legible to the rest of the company. It suits an engineer who finds correctness under constraint more interesting than shipping the next screen.

Own the data layer

Design data models that make tenant isolation and data classification structural rather than conventional.
Run migrations on live systems without downtime or data loss, including the large and awkward ones.

Handle the operational reality of multi-region — consistency, latency, deploys, and debugging something that only reproduces in one region.
Own the API surface
Design public APIs that are coherent, predictable, and pleasant to integrate against.
Own versioning, deprecation, and backwards compatibility. Customers do not upgrade on your schedule.
Build the authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and idempotency behavior that production APIs need.

Meet regularly with the Hospice nursing staff to review problems or unique issues from caseloads; share professional support; and exchange feedback aimed toward enhancing professional growth

Supervise and document the NAC every two weeks or as assigned
Inform the Patient Care Coordinator of unusual or potentially problematic patient/family issues
Assume the role of associate nurse when responding to patient/loved ones/caregivers of other primary nurses during off-hour times or as requested by the Patient Care Coordinator to fill patient/family needs during the absence of other primary nurses

Participate in the Hospice orientation and in-service training programs for professional staff

description:
Who we are:
Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Visit
gomotive.com
to learn more.
About the Role:
Motive is looking for a Senior Commissions Forecasting & Sales Compensation Program Lead. The primary responsibility is to own the commissions modeling, forecast and related analysis in an FP&A-partnering planning process: establish the methodology, maintain the model, collect and validate inputs, produce forecast submissions, explain variances, and provide decision-ready commentary to Finance and business leadership.
The role also assists in designs, operationalization, and continuously improving global sales compensation programs. It sits at the intersection of FP&A, Sales, GTM Strategy and Operations, Finance, People, Legal, Payroll, and Business Technology.
The successful candidate will turn complex business objectives into a reliable, explainable commissions forecast and clear, scalable, auditable compensation programs. They will own the commissions forecasting process, including the forecast calendar, model architecture, assumptions, run-rate methodology, headcount and plan-change inputs, source-data validation, forecast submissions, actuals-to-forecast analysis, forecast-to-plan analysis, and executive-ready commentary. They will also evaluate plan mechanics, identify unintended incentives or payout risk, build analytical models, document policy intent, lead cross-functional decisions, and ensure approved changes are translated accurately into systems, communications, and operating processes.
This is a high-impact individual-contributor role for someone who can move comfortably between FP&A forecasting, strategic design discussions, detailed modeling, policy language, system requirements, and field-facing explanation. This role partners closely with our GTM & Corporate FP&A teams along with our Sales Operations teams. The role must understand how plan mechanics, headcount, attainment, hiring timing, ramping, quota changes, and payout behavior affect forecast accuracy, cost, seller behavior, payout experience, and operational risk.
What You'll Do:
Own the end-to-end commissions forecast process in partnership with FP&A and sales ops, including forecast calendar, model structure, assumptions, source data, submissions, and change control.
Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual commissions forecasts and explain actuals-to-forecast and forecast-to-plan variances by segment, role, plan component, headcount movement, attainment, and timing.
Establish forecast inputs and operating rhythms with Sales Ops, Finance, People, Payroll, and business leaders; document ownership, deadlines, assumptions, and evidence.
Assist in the design and evolution of sales compensation plans across multiple segments, roles, geographies, and pay periods.
Translate GTM strategy into measurable compensation mechanics, including quotas, crediting rules, accelerators, kickers, draws, SPIFFs, MBOs, ramping structures, and exception frameworks.
Build models and scenario analyses to evaluate plan outcomes, behavioral incentives, fairness, payout volatility, cost implications, and implementation complexity.
Partner with Sales Leadership, GTM Strategy and Operations, Finance, People, Legal, Payroll, and Business Technology to align on requirements, tradeoffs, approvals, and timing.
Co-own the compensation-design workstream for major programs such as annual-plan redesigns, new-product incentives, role or segment changes, and compensation-system migrations.
Convert approved design decisions into clear business requirements, decision logs, process documentation, test cases, and implementation-ready specifications.
Review system outputs and reporting for alignment to policy and intended plan behavior; identify root causes when results are inaccurate, delayed, or difficult for sellers to understand.
Establish practical governance for plan changes, exceptions, approvals, and effective dates, with a clear audit trail.
Create and deliver enablement for sales leaders, managers, and compensation partners; explain complex mechanics clearly and confidently.
Develop recurring performance reporting on attainment, payout behavior, plan participation, exception themes, forecast accuracy, and compensation-program effectiveness.
Partner with FP&A on forecast submissions, executive commentary, scenario analysis, and reconciliation of forecast assumptions to approved plan design and operating data.
Improve the seller and manager experience through clearer plan documents, better statements, self-service resources, office hours, and better intake processes.
Support audit and IPO-readiness activities by ensuring that plan logic, approvals, controls, and evidence are complete and reusable.
Mentor analysts and collaborate with systems and operations partners without having formal people-management responsibility.
What We're Looking For:
6+ years of experience in FP&A, sales compensation, incentive compensation, sales operations, revenue operations, finance, or a closely related analytical discipline, including meaningful ownership of commissions or variable-compensation forecasting.
Demonstrated experience designing or materially changing sales compensation plans in a complex, multi-segment organization.
Strong FP&A, analytical, and financial-modeling skills; able to work comfortably with large datasets and build transparent forecast, bridge, variance, and scenario models.
Deep understanding of compensation mechanics such as quota allocation, attainment, crediting, accelerators, kickers, draws, ramping, clawbacks, SPIFFs, and exception handling.
Experience partnering with FP&A and senior stakeholders and building consensus across Sales, Finance, Operations, People, and Technology.
Ability to write clear policy language, business requirements, process documentation, and executive-ready recommendations.
Strong systems orientation and experience with an incentive compensation management platform such as Xactly, Varicent, CaptivateIQ, Everstage, Anaplan, or an equivalent system.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain complex compensation mechanics to non-specialists.
High ownership, attention to detail, sound judgment, and comfort operating in ambiguous, high-change environments.
Preferred qualifications
Experience supporting a global SaaS, technology, or subscription business.
Experience with Salesforce, Workday, Snowflake, SQL, or business-intelligence tools.
Experience designing compensation for both new-logo and account-management organizations.
Experience creating enablement programs, compensation hubs, FAQs, or self-service resources.
